q: Hajduk Split were founded in 1911 by a group of Split students who were studying in which city?
hint: Four students from Split, studying in Prague, took the idea home and founded the club on 13 February 1911 — the name means 'outlaw' or 'bandit', for the rebels who fought Ottoman rule.

q: Hajduk Split were re-formed in 1944 on which Adriatic island, becoming the official football team of the Yugoslav resistance?
hint: With the Adriatic islands serving as a haven for the resistance, the club was reborn on Vis on 7 May 1944 and its players joined the Partisan general headquarters there.

q: Which British prime minister's son was present when Hajduk Split were re-formed on Vis in 1944?
hint: Randolph Churchill, Winston's son, was among the British officers present alongside Partisan leader Josip Broz Tito on 7 May 1944.

q: In September 1944 Hajduk Split played the British Army in Bari in front of around 40,000 spectators — how did it end?
hint: A heavy 9-2 defeat on 23 September 1944, in front of a crowd that dwarfed anything the club had played before.

q: Hajduk Split have reached two European semi-finals: the 1973 Cup Winners' Cup and which competition in 1984?
hint: The 1984 UEFA Cup run took in Metz, VfB Stuttgart, Torino, Dnipro and Universitatea Craiova before the semi-final.

q: Which player is Hajduk Split's all-time leading scorer, with 729 goals for the club?
hint: Frane Matošić scored 729 goals in 739 matches. Vedran Rožić holds the official appearance record with 390.

q: Which future Shakhtar Donetsk and Croatia captain began his senior career at Hajduk Split?
hint: Srna left Split for Shakhtar in 2003 and stayed 15 years, becoming their record appearance holder and captaining Croatia over 130 times.

q: Hajduk Split's supporters' group, founded in 1950, holds which distinction?
o: The oldest organised supporters' group in Europe
The first group officially recognised by UEFA
The largest single supporters' group in Europe
The first to be given its own stand
hint: Founded on 28 October 1950 by three students in Zagreb — Ante Dorić, Ante Ivanišević and Vjenceslav Žuvela — a day before a decisive match against Red Star Belgrade.

q: Hajduk Split's supporters' group took its name from a fan movement in which country?
hint: The founders had seen the Brazilian torcida at the 1950 World Cup; the word comes from the Portuguese verb 'torcer', to cheer on.

q: What made Hajduk Split's 1950 Yugoslav championship remarkable?
o: They won it without losing a single match
They won it with an all-teenage side
They won it after starting with nine defeats
They won it while playing every match away
hint: An unbeaten league title that no Yugoslav club matched in the 40 years before the league broke up.

q: Which stadium has been Hajduk Split's home since 1979?
hint: The 33,987-seat Poljud, with Torcida massed in the north stand. Maksimir is Dinamo Zagreb's ground in the capital.

q: Along with Hajduk Split, Dinamo Zagreb and Red Star Belgrade, which club made up the 'Big Four' of Yugoslav football?
hint: The four dominated SFR Yugoslavia between them; Partizan also reached the 1966 European Cup final.
